comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: 2026-10-24: on main in 4051ffb4 and 421c4707. Each candidate is named by a ref that reaches it alone; a participant with no pane gets the new shadowed refusal. With --group, a name several agents answer to means the group's one member (post path only).

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Seen 2026-10-19 on 0.17.0, devenv. A Codex member of a directed council group was added by pane id, then joined as `review`. The director's `muster msg post --group <group> --to review -` was refused: `review could be p2c3tkry84 or review; say which, by one of those`. `review` is what was typed, so one of the two suggestions repeats the failing input, and p2c3tkry84 is a pane outside the group. `--to <the member's pane id>` worked.

The refusal could name each candidate by a ref that resolves to it alone, as `docs/cli/msg.md` says one does (a pane id, or `name@machine`), never the bare name (`Refusal::WhichParticipant` in `crates/muster-daemon/src/messages/mod.rs`). And with `--group` given, `--to` could prefer that group's members, so a pane outside the group with the same name does not make it ambiguous. Whether that rule is right is open, since the same `--to` would then mean different agents in different groups.

How a pane outside the group came to be called `review` while a participant held that name is not known. a_2hKgI2Qj7 (done) refuses that for `pane new --name` and `pane rename`; a_2hKMo9s9t (done) covers a pane and a participant of one name that are the same agent.
title: An ambiguous --to offers the typed name itself as one way to say which
